title: Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s
seo_title: Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s – Primary 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count in 2s, 5s and 10s; count groups of objects; find missing numbers in counting patterns. (summary of the NERDC Primary 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 maths worksheets on counting in 2s, 5s and 10s with pictures of pairs, hands and bundles, groups and counting stories. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Add the same number each time
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
  • Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20.
  • Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40.

Examples

Example

How many eyes do 4 children have?

2, 4, 6, 8

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting in 1sJump by the same number.
Missing a jumpCount the groups too.
Stopping too soonCount every group.

items.q: How many socks? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. There are 6 socks.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 8 + 2 = 10. 9 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many eyes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each child has 2 eyes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 eyes.

items.q: How many shoes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 shoes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 shoes.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 16 + 2 = 18. 17 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many socks? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 10 socks.

items.q: Count in 2s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. When you count in 2s from 0, every number is even. 7, 9 and 15 are odd.

items.q: Count in 2s. What number is missing?
How many eyes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each child has 2 eyes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. There are 12 eyes.

items.q: Count back in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 less. 16 − 2 = 14. 15 is counting back in 1s.

items.q: How many shoes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 shoes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. There are 14 shoes.

items.q: How many socks? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. There are 18 socks.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 28 + 2 = 30. 29 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Count in 2s. What number is missing?
Count in 2s from 0. Which number do you NOT say?
Count in 5s. What comes next? 5, 10, 15, 20, ?
items.e: Add 5 each time: 20 + 5 = 25.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next? 2, 4, 6, 8, ?
items.e: Add 2 each time: 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next? 25, 30, 35, 40, ?
items.e: Add 5 each time: 40 + 5 = 45.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next? 12, 14, 16, 18, ?
items.e: Add 2 each time: 18 + 2 = 20.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next? 30, 40, 50, 60, ?
items.e: Add 10 each time: 60 + 10 = 70.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10. There are 10 fingers.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 15 + 5 = 20. 16 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. There are 15 fingers.

items.q: How many petals? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each flower has 5 petals. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 petals.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 40 + 5 = 45. 41 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Count in 5s from 0. How do the numbers end?
items.e: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 … The last digit goes 0, 5, 0, 5. So they always end in 0 or 5.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 fingers.

items.q: Count in 5s. What number is missing?
How many petals? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each flower has 5 petals. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. There are 25 petals.

items.q: Count back in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 less. 40 − 5 = 35. 39 is counting back in 1s.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. There are 30 fingers.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 65 + 5 = 70. 66 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Count in 5s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: Counting in 5s, every number ends in 0 or 5. 45 ends in 5. 42, 54 and 48 do not.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 95 + 5 = 100. 96 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Count in 5s up to 25. How many 5s do you count?
items.e: Say the numbers: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 5 numbers, so there are 5 fives in 25.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next? 8, 10, 12, 14, ?
items.e: Add 2 each time: 14 + 2 = 16.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next? 50, 60, 70, 80, ?
items.e: Add 10 each time: 80 + 10 = 90.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next? 60, 70, 80, 90, ?
items.e: Add 10 each time: 90 + 10 = 100.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next? 4, 6, 8, 10, ?
items.e: Add 2 each time: 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next? 10, 15, 20, 25, ?
items.e: Add 5 each time: 25 + 5 = 30.

items.q: Each stick has 10 cubes. How many cubes?
items.e: Each stick has 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. There are 30 cubes.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 30 + 10 = 40. 31 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 10s.
items.e: Each child shows 2 hands. That is 10 fingers. Count in 10s: 10, 20. There are 20 fingers.

items.q: Each ten frame is full. How many counters?
items.e: A full ten frame has 10 counters. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. There are 50 counters.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 60 + 10 = 70. 61 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Each stick has 10 cubes. How many cubes?
items.e: Each stick has 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. There are 60 cubes.

items.q: Which one counts in 10s?
items.e: Counting in 10s, each number is 10 more: 20, 30, 40. 20, 21, 22 is 1s, 20, 22, 24 is 2s and 20, 25, 30 is 5s.

items.q: Count in 10s. What number is missing?
How many fingers? Count in 10s.
items.e: Each child shows 2 hands. That is 10 fingers. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. There are 30 fingers.

items.q: Count back in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 less. 70 − 10 = 60. 69 is counting back in 1s.

items.q: Each ten frame is full. How many counters?
items.e: A full ten frame has 10 counters. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. There are 40 counters.

items.q: How many 10s make 50?
items.e: Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. That is 5 tens.

items.q: Each stick has 10 cubes. How many cubes?
items.e: Each stick has 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80. There are 80 cubes.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 90 + 10 = 100. 91 is counting in 1s.

items.q: What is 10 more than 40?
items.e: Count on one 10 from 40: 50. 41 is only 1 more. 30 is 10 less.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next? 15, 20, 25, 30, ?
items.e: Add 5 each time: 30 + 5 = 35.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next? 30, 35, 40, 45, ?
items.e: Add 5 each time: 45 + 5 = 50.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next? 10, 12, 14, 16, ?
items.e: Add 2 each time: 16 + 2 = 18.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next? 20, 30, 40, 50, ?
items.e: Add 10 each time: 50 + 10 = 60.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next? 20, 25, 30, 35, ?
items.e: Add 5 each time: 35 + 5 = 40.

items.q: 4 groups of 2. How many counters altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 8 altogether.
There are 3 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. That is 15 altogether.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the circles, not the apples. There are 5 groups, with 2 in each group.
Look inside one circle. It has 5 stars. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many counters? Count in 5s.
items.e: There are 2 rows. Each row has 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10. That is 10.
There are 2 groups of 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20. That is 20 altogether.
There are 4 rows. Each row has 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 8.

items.q: 6 groups of 2. How many apples altogether?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 12 altogether.
There are 3 lots of 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. That is 30 altogether.
There are 3 rows. Each row has 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. That is 15.

items.q: 4 groups of 5. How many counters altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20 altogether.
Count the circles, not the stars. There are 4 groups, with 5 in each group.
There are 2 rows. Each row has 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20. That is 20.

items.q: How many counters? Count in 2s.
items.e: There are 5 rows. Each row has 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 10.
There are 4 lots of 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. That is 40 altogether.
There are 4 rows. Each row has 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 20.

items.q: How many cubes are there? Each tall rod is 1 ten.
items.e: 5 tens and 3 units make 53.
6 tens and 4 units make 64.
6 tens and 2 units make 62.

items.q: How many cubes are there? Each tall rod is 1 ten.
items.e: 5 tens and 8 units make 58.

items.q: Share 6 sweets equally between 2 plates. How many on each plate?
items.e: Give 1 to each plate, then again, until none are left. Each plate gets 3. Check: 3 + 3 = 6.
Give 1 to each plate, then again, until none are left. Each plate gets 5. Check: 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: Share 8 sweets equally between 2 plates. How many on each plate?
items.e: Give 1 to each plate, then again, until none are left. Each plate gets 4. Check: 4 + 4 = 8.
Give 1 to each plate, then again, until none are left. Each plate gets 4. Check: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

items.q: A bike has 2 wheels. How many wheels do 3 bikes have?
items.e: Count in 2s for the wheels: 2, 4, 6. There are 6 wheels.
Give 1 to each plate, then again, until none are left. Each plate gets 10. Check: 10 + 10 = 20.
Count in 5s, one bag at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20. Temi has 20 apples.
Give 1 to each plate, then again, until none are left. Each plate gets 5. Check: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: A box has 10 pencils. How many pencils are in 3 boxes?
items.e: Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. There are 30 pencils.

items.q: Chiamaka shares 10 biscuits with Joy. They get the same. How many each?
items.e: Share 10 into 2 equal groups: 5 and 5. They get 5 each. Check: 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: Each child has 2 hands. How many hands do 5 children have?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. 5 children have 10 hands.
Give 1 to each plate, then again, until none are left. Each plate gets 8. Check: 8 + 8 = 16.

items.q: 5 children sit at each table. There are 4 tables. How many children?
items.e: Count in 5s, one table at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 children.

items.q: Amaka shares 20 stickers equally between 4 friends. How many does each friend get?
items.e: Give 1 to each friend, again and again. Each friend gets 5. Check: 5, 10, 15, 20.

items.q: Ifeoma has 7 pairs of socks. How many socks is that?
items.e: A pair is 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 14 socks.

items.q: 12 children get into groups of 2. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count in 2s until you reach 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 groups.
Count in 5s, one bag at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20. Ruth has 20 apples.

items.q: Esther shares 10 biscuits with Chioma. They get the same. How many each?
items.e: Share 10 into 2 equal groups: 5 and 5. They get 5 each. Check: 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: Babatunde shares 20 stickers equally between 4 friends. How many does each friend get?
items.e: Give 1 to each friend, again and again. Each friend gets 5. Check: 5, 10, 15, 20.

items.q: Kayode has 7 pairs of socks. How many socks is that?
items.e: A pair is 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 14 socks.
